(Right) This workspace is built once and repeatedly used to answer different queries.

header: 2Librarian Agents: Agent Curated Filesystems as Anticipatory Workspaces

images.caption: Figure 2:MDP Definition of Librarian Agents.Starting from a raw list of documents, a builder agent can create a workspace with four actions:Create,Merge,Delete, andStop. An answering agent navigates the resulting workspace through file-listing and file-reading actions, produces a response, and receives a task-specific correctness score. Here, we depict an augmented workspace from the BrowseComp-Plus dataset.

Figure 3:Dense Rewards via Probes.We train the builder agent with RL to directly maximize performance of answering agent. To densify the reward, the builder agent operates over workspace augmentations and is rewarded for change in accuracy. Probes to the answering agent are done at regular intervals (8 turns) up to the maximum horizonHH.

Figure 4:Results on BrowseComp-Plus.We compare Librarian Agents against RAG, Caching and Builder-Based Memory baselines using two answering agent models (Qwen 3.5 4B and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite). We find that Librarian Agents significantly outperforms all methods for both answering agents.

Figure 5:Qualitative comparison of RL and base building.On BrowseComp-Plus, the base model creates a fragmented filesystem that is difficult for the answering agent to navigate, whereas the RL-trained builder surfaces relevant information in dedicated files and produces a richer, more ergonomic organization.

Figure 6:BrowseComp-Plus reuse curves.Left: recorded construction and navigation tokens per query. Right: recorded tokens per expected correct answer after normalization by observed full-denominator accuracy. Shaded regions show paired corpus-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals.

Figure 7:Recovery on BrowseComp-Plus using provenance information.When the synthetic filesystem omitted a required detail, the answering agent followed provenance links to the relevant raw source and recovered the correct answer.
Figure 8:Training curve for the BrowseComp-Plus builder.Aggregate rollout reward during GRPO training, smoothed with an exponential moving average.
